title: Baba Ganoush
subtitle: Smoky roasted aubergine dip
excerpt: Baba ganoush is a Middle Eastern dip made from aubergines charred directly over a flame or under a grill until the flesh inside turns sweet and smoky. The charred skins are discarded and the flesh is mixed with garlic, lemon, and olive oil. The smokiness is everything.
sourceNotes: Baba ganoush is eaten across the Levant -- Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Israel, and Palestine -- as well as Egypt and Turkey. The name translates loosely as pampered daddy in Arabic. The key technique is charring the whole aubergine so the flesh takes on a deep, smoky flavour.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made 2 days ahead. Keep refrigerated. The flavour deepens overnight.

content.text: Charring over an open gas flame gives the deepest smoky flavour. If you do not have a gas hob, use the highest grill setting and position the aubergines as close to the element as possible. The skin must be fully charred and the inside must be completely soft.

Place the whole aubergines directly over a gas flame on medium-high heat. Turn every 4 to 5 minutes using tongs until the skin is charred all over and the aubergine feels very soft when pressed. This takes 20 to 25 minutes total.
Transfer to a colander. Leave to cool for 10 minutes. The steam will continue to soften the flesh.
Cut the aubergines open lengthways. Scoop out the flesh with a spoon. Discard the charred skins.
Place the flesh in a sieve over a bowl. Let it drain for 5 minutes to remove excess water. This prevents a watery dip.
Chop the drained flesh roughly, then mix with the garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, and salt. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Transfer to a serving dish. Drizzle with more olive oil. Scatter over the parsley. Serve with flatbread or vegetables.

items.cause: Flesh not drained long enough after cooking
items.fix: Always drain in a sieve for at least 5 minutes and press gently to remove excess liquid

items.cause: Aubergines were roasted in the oven rather than charred over a flame
items.fix: For smoke, you need direct contact with the heat source -- gas flame or a very hot grill

items.cause: Raw garlic is very sharp in a cold dip
items.fix: Use only 1 clove for a milder result, or roast the garlic first to soften its bite

content.text: Baba ganoush belongs to the meze table -- the spread of small dishes that opens a meal across the Levant, Egypt, and Turkey. It is always served at room temperature. In Lebanon it is made with tahini, which gives it a nutty richness. In Egypt it is plainer, dressed simply with olive oil.
